clue.text: Party politics covers up blunder

indicators.note: the opening phrase hides, or covers up, a short run of letters straddling its two words

explanation.surface: A party's political manoeuvring hides its own mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a small blunder in typing or typesetting.

clue.text: Beaten mid-clue by setter's ultimate instrument

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked about and battered out of shape, so the letters of mid-clue are rearranged
ultimate means last, so the final letter of setter's is taken

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that a mid-clue position was bettered by their final instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaten' rearranges MIDCLUE into DULCIME; 'ultimate' adds R, the last letter of setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: A dulcimer is a stringed musical instrument struck with small hammers.

clue.text: Losing against obscure illness

indicators.note: losing says the second piece is dropped from the first

parts.note: obscure means unclear, vague
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: An obscure illness that someone is losing the battle against.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing' takes V out of VAGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fever with shivering fits, an old word for malarial illness.

clue.text: Stuart A. played with Yes, the rock group?

indicators.note: played suggests the letters of Stuart A. are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: Y is a common abbreviation for yes, as on a Y/N form

explanation.surface: Stuart A., a musician, jammed with the prog band Yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' rearranges STUARTA into STATUAR. 'Rock group' poses as a band, but it means a group of figures carved from stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Statuary is statues collectively, a group of sculptures often carved from stone.

clue.text: Make a pitch: "Hull's location is on the up, rather flamboyant"

indicators.note: in a down clue, on the up means the piece reads upwards, so its letters are turned round

parts.note: Hull is a port in the north-east of England, NE
camp means theatrical and rather flamboyant

explanation.surface: A sales pitch for Hull: the city is on the rise and rather flashy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the up' turns NE into EN. Hull is a port city in Yorkshire, in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: To encamp is to set up a camp, that is pitch tents.

clue.text: I agree, Terry's worried about Nuneaton centre's past

parts.note: yes is what one says to agree

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged name surrounds the centre letters
worried means troubled or shaken up, so the letters of Terry are rearranged

parts.note: the 's stands for is, so only the name is used

indicators.note: the centre of Nuneaton is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that Terry is anxious about the past of Nuneaton's town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges the name into TERYR, which 'about' wraps round the middle pair to give TERYEAR. Nuneaton is a town in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesteryear means time gone by, the past, as in songs of yesteryear.

clue.text: Fate is cold and reluctant before love

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
loth means reluctant or unwilling
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone's fate is to stay cold and hesitant about falling in love.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the three Fates spin, measure and cut the thread of life.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho is the one of the three Greek Fates who spins the thread of life.

clue.text: See 26
Solvers no good as babies?

parts.note: the setter addresses those solving as you

explanation.surface: A setter teasingly asks whether the solvers are as useless as infants.
explanation.definitionFit: Young as a collective noun means offspring, the babies of an animal.

clue.text: Mole, a musician getting ready to enthral a king's mistress?

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: a musician getting ready tunes up, so is a tuner
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: A spy, a musician, preparing to captivate a royal mistress.
explanation.walkthrough: Nell Gwyn was an actress and mistress of England's King Charles II. 'Mole' looks like a spy but means a burrowing animal or digger.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole digs tunnels underground, so is a natural burrower or digger.

clue.text: Pit workers possibly round river front — god!

parts.note: O is round in shape
R is the map abbreviation for river
the chest is the front of the body
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Miners circle a river bank and exclaim in shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pit workers' suggests miners; it means players in the orchestra pit of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The orchestra plays in the pit below a theatre stage, so its musicians work there.

clue.text: Virginia's classic direction of keeper going to work?

definitions.text: Virginia's classic direction of keeper going to work?

parts.words: Virginia's classic direction of keeper going to work?
parts.note: a novel by Virginia Woolf whose title reads as the route a coastal light's keeper takes to work

explanation.surface: Virginia's famous route for a keeper heading off to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of Virginia Woolf's 1927 novel reads literally as where a lamp keeper on the coast is headed.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf wrote this classic novel, whose title is also a keeper's commute.

clue.text: State's contribution to ransom, a liability

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A country's share of a ransom payment becomes a debt it must carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Somalia is a country in the Horn of Africa, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Small weak person liable to get lit up

definitions.meaning: a small firework that is set alight

explanation.surface: A feeble little man prone to getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lit up' suggests drunk, but here it means set alight, as a firework is.
explanation.definitionFit: Squib means both a small firework and a puny, insignificant person.

clue.text: See 12
Former president's protective of society people

indicators.note: being protective of something means wrapping round it, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: Juan Peron was a former president of Argentina

explanation.surface: A former president is protective of high society's people.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan Perón was president of Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: Persons is a formal plural meaning individuals, that is people.

clue.text: One could be wrapped up in this Walsh novel

definitions.text: One could be wrapped up in this

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters of Walsh take a new order

explanation.surface: A reader could be absorbed in this novel by an author called Walsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it signals the rearrangement. 'wrapped up in' suggests absorbed in reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl is a large cloth draped round the shoulders, so a person is wrapped in it.

clue.text: Reverse the setting up of one vulgar doctor

parts.note: 'un is a colloquial form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
to doctor is to tamper with or rig

explanation.surface: An instruction to undo the appointment of a coarse physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb: to rig or falsify.
explanation.definitionFit: To unrig a ship is to strip it of the rigging that was set up.

clue.text: Lad, the almost disappearing one

indicators.note: disappearing says the second piece vanishes from the first

parts.note: a lad is a youth

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is missing

explanation.surface: A boy who is nearly vanishing from sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims THE to TH, and 'disappearing' removes TH from YOUTH. 'one' is the impersonal pronoun, as in 'one never knows'.
explanation.definitionFit: The impersonal one can be replaced by the general you: one never knows, you never know.

clue.text: Parking in sporting run range not established

indicators.note: in says the first piece goes inside the shuffled word
sporting suggests the word run is playing about, so its letters are mixed

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
a range is a kitchen stove or oven

explanation.surface: A parking spot inside a sports running track whose range has yet to be confirmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' mixes RUN into UNR, with P put 'in' to make UNPR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unproven has not been demonstrated or established as true.

clue.text: Who's part of the movie host's run?

definitions.text: Who's part of the movie host
definitions.meaning: a person who is one of the crowd in a film, a host meaning a multitude
in cricket a run scored without being hit off the bat, such as a wide

explanation.walkthrough: 'host' means a large crowd, not a presenter. In cricket, byes and wides are runs added to the total.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is both a film background player and a cricket run not scored off the bat.

clue.text: Believing it's involved with ethics

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so the two sets of letters are mixed up as one

parts.note: the 's stands for is, so only it gives letters

explanation.surface: Faith is bound up with morality.
explanation.definitionFit: Theistic means holding a belief in God or gods, so believing.

clue.text: Benjamin, a familiar national figure?

parts.note: Brit is the familiar, informal word for a British national
ten is a number, a figure

explanation.surface: Someone named Benjamin is a well-known British personality.
explanation.walkthrough: Benjamin Britten was an English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin is the first name of the composer, so it names him by his given name.

clue.text: Setter's married a foreign female — so complaint impossible?

parts.note: the setter says I am, shortened to I'm
une is French for a, in its feminine form

explanation.surface: The setter wed a woman from abroad, so has no grounds for grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests grumbling but means an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone immune cannot catch a disease, so an ailment or complaint is impossible.

clue.text: Lower than the lowest turned up as rain producer

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the pieces read upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: sub means under or below
min is short for minimum, the lowest

explanation.surface: Something lower than the bottom flipped upwards and brought rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SUBMIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a dark grey cloud bringing rain.

clue.text: Almost express contentment with chamber music man

indicators.note: almost means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a cat purrs to express contentment
a cell is a small chamber or room

explanation.surface: A man nearly purring with satisfaction over chamber music.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Purcell was an English Baroque composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Purcell was a composer, so a man of music.

clue.text: Not much of a role for top actor of advanced circle

definitions.text: Not much of a role for top actor

parts.note: came means moved forward, advanced
O is circular in shape

explanation.surface: A star from the advanced acting circle gets only a small part.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief film part, often played by a famous star.

clue.text: Meteor and small copper rocks occur as predicted

indicators.note: rocks means shakes, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: Cu is the short chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A meteor and a small piece of copper are space rocks arriving just as forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' looks like a noun but is the verb, shaking up METEOR and CU together.
explanation.definitionFit: When a prophecy is fulfilled it is said to have happened as foretold.

clue.text: Low density rock, possibly providing a background for hotel lobbies?

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
D is the symbol for density
rock is one example of music

explanation.surface: Light, dense rock perhaps gives a backdrop to hotel entrance halls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective but is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mood music is gentle background playing, the kind piped into hotel lobbies.

clue.text: Star-struck followers of old lady with judo outfit

parts.note: old lady is slang for mother, ma
a gi is the uniform worn for judo

explanation.surface: Fans of a mother in her martial-arts kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star-struck' suggests awed fans; the wise men followed the star of Bethlehem.
explanation.definitionFit: The Magi were the wise men who followed the star to Bethlehem.

clue.text: The gang gloated

definitions.meaning: a team or band of people working together
an old past tense of crow, to boast or gloat

explanation.definitionFit: Crew is a group of workers, and also an archaic past tense of crow.

clue.text: Less complicated clue in lower case

parts.note: minus means less, as in five minus two

indicators.note: complicated means tangled, so the letters of clue are mixed

explanation.surface: A simpler clue printed in small letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges CLUE into CULE.
explanation.definitionFit: Minuscule script is small letters, as opposed to capitals.

clue.text: Fine for Scots to have English escort

parts.note: guid is the Scots spelling of good, fine

explanation.surface: A fine for Scots to employ an English chaperone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like a penalty but means good.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide someone is to lead or escort them.
